title: U.S. House · Texas's 5th District
area: Kaufman, Van Zandt, and part of Dallas and Smith counties, east of Dallas

context.text: Incumbent Lance Gooden (R) ran unopposed in the March 3, 2026 Republican primary. Chelsey Hockett won a Democratic primary runoff against Ruth Torres on May 26, 2026.

candidates.name: Lance Gooden

summary.text: Lance Gooden is the Republican incumbent U.S. Representative for Texas's 5th Congressional District. A Terrell resident who worked in the insurance industry, he served three terms in the Texas House before his 2018 election to Congress, where he sits on the Judiciary and Armed Services committees.

background.text: Born in Nashville, Tennessee, in 1982; according to Wikipedia he was raised in Terrell, Texas, in Kaufman County.
Earned a bachelor's degree in finance and government from the University of Texas in 2004.
Worked as an insurance broker and risk-management consultant; his official biography says he spent 10 years in the insurance industry.

Served in the Texas House of Representatives (District 4, covering parts of Henderson and Kaufman counties) from 2011 to 2015 and from 2017 to 2019, three terms in all; Wikipedia reports he lost the 2014 Republican primary before returning to the seat in 2016.
First elected to Congress in 2018 and took office January 3, 2019, succeeding Jeb Hensarling. His district stretches from Dallas County to Henderson, Kaufman, Van Zandt, Wood and Upshur counties.
In the 119th Congress he serves on the House Judiciary Committee and the House Armed Services Committee.
According to his official biography, he lives in Terrell with his wife, Alexa, and their two children.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on the Judiciary (including the Courts, Intellectual Property, Artificial Intelligence, and the Internet Subcommittee) and the House Committee on Armed Services in the 2025–2026 Congress.

candidates.researchNotes: No Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey or curated key-messages profile was found for Gooden in this race's coverage; positions on specific issues were not documented from the sources checked.

candidates.name: Chelsey Hockett
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 26, 2026 Democratic primary runoff against Ruth Torres

summary.text: Chelsey Hockett is the Democratic nominee for Texas's 5th Congressional District and describes herself as a mother of two and community organizer, not a career politician. She has worked in restaurants and for airlines and has been involved with the Kaufman County Democratic Party. Her campaign emphasizes health care, public schools, labor and reproductive rights.

background.text: Born in Frederick, Maryland, where she says she lived as a child; attended Marcus High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Texas Woman's University in 2015.

Her career experience includes working in restaurants, for airlines, and as a stay-at-home parent. In her Ballotpedia survey she says her first job, at age 15, was as a rescue technician at a veterinary clinic.
According to her campaign website, she lives in Terrell, Texas, is a mother of two, and comes from a union family.
Has been affiliated with the Kaufman County Democratic Party. Her campaign website describes her organizing with friends, working with local Democrats, speaking at meetings and protesting.
Advanced to a Democratic primary runoff after the March 3, 2026 primary and won the May 26, 2026 runoff over Ruth Torres. She describes herself as not a career politician.

priorities.text: Says she will fight for fair wages, affordable healthcare, and cost-of-living relief for working families.
Says she supports well-funded public schools, safe communities, and what she describes as a "humane border system."

positions.summary: Says she believes in reproductive freedom.
positions.quote: I believe in reproductive freedom, immigrant rights, strong unions, fully funded public schools, and a government that actually works for the people who live here.

positions.summary: Says healthcare is a human right and supports expanding healthcare access.
positions.quote: I believe healthcare is a human right.
